newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: OPSM says studies potential purchases.
newsitem.headline: OPSM says studies potential purchases.

text.p: Protective equipment and eyewear maker OPSM Protector Ltd said on Thursday it was examining potential acquisitions up to A$70 million, mainly for its Protector Technology division.

OPSM was looking at targets from A$10 million up and could easily handle a debt-funded acquisition up to A$70 million, given its conservative balance sheet, managing director Jeff Kelly told reporters after a Securities Institute of Australia briefing.
Kelly also said he was comfortable with a previous forecast of a full year profit improvement of about 10 percent.
"I think it will be around that sort of figure," he said.

Possible acquisitions were seen mainly in Europe and the U.S. as these were the two major markets for the Protector Technologies business, which designs and makes protective equipment and safety systems.
"(Protector Technologies) is where we need to attain more critical mass ... we're probably looking at little more slowly in the other areas," he
Asked about the possibility of taking the OPSM eyewear and eyecare division offshore, Kelly said New Zealand had been very successful for the group.
"We are examining some other possibilities offshore but being very cautious about it," he said.
Analysts are forecasting OPSM will report a full year profit to June 30, 1997 of between A$28.5 million and A$29.6 million, compared with a pre-abnormals 1995/96 profit of A$25.6 million.
